title: S&H FX 2 — approximate patch and estimated MIDI
method: Long-window FFT and spectrogram analysis separates persistent pitch families from the stepped moving resonances. The source supports approximate G3/D4/A4, G3/Bb3/D4/F4, and F3/A3/C4/E4/G4 voicings. The MIDI holds those estimated chords while the new software patch generates sample-and-hold filter motion. Exact original trigger count, octave allocation, gates, and random modulation are not recoverable.
uncertainties: Original performance MIDI and recording-specific factory SysEx are unavailable. This is an estimated audio reconstruction, not an exact original performance or authenticated factory patch.
Every note-on velocity is fixed to 100 as an explicit unknown placeholder; note-off velocity is 64. These values were not recovered from the audio.
Played-key octave and voicing are conditional on the newly designed patch. The hardware oscillator tuning, system transpose, original key presses, controller changes, and effect history are unknown.
Onsets refer to the decoded public MP3. MP3 encoder delay, hardware latency, recording processing, exact gates, and release tails are not recovered.
These are estimated held voicings supported by pitch families, not exact recovered MIDI. Oscillator intervals could change the number and octave of the original keys.
Original S&H state, phase, rate, controller activity, and effect history are unavailable; stochastic motion cannot be expected to align with the MP3.
The later five-note chord may include a mixture of held notes and release tails. The chosen common gate is a rendering assumption.

patch_design.name: APX SH FX2
rationale: Slightly detuned saw oscillators preserve the stable chord families.
A resonant filter driven by sample-and-hold LFO approximates the changing blocks of spectral energy.
A slower filter/amplitude LFO and soft attack/release approximate the broader swells without inventing original controller messages.
uncertainties: These are newly designed software parameters informed by the public demo, not recovered Roland factory settings.
No authentic factory dump or controlled hardware measurements exist for this comparison.
The random sequence and all filter/LFO settings are newly voiced software choices. The resulting motion is intentionally an approximation, not a reproduction of the hardware random state.
